docs.title: PIMS Requirements Baseline
docs.text:
Post Import Management System — Consolidated requirements for Defra EU Imports risk assessment and post-import check management.

PIMS is a Dynamics 365 Model-Driven App used by EU Imports caseworkers to receive, risk-assess, and schedule post-import checks on animal and commodity consignments entering the UK from the EU. It integrates with TRACES Classic (ITAHC/DOCOM) and IPAFFS (Importer Notifications) via Azure Integration Services.

docs.title: About this baseline
docs.text:
This site is the consolidated, deduplicated and traceable requirements baseline for PIMS. It was reconstructed from the original requirement records (referenced throughout as IMTA-nnnn) and from the current implementation, and consolidates 65 source records into 47 user stories.

Where the source records and the implementation disagreed, the implementation was taken as the source of truth. Statements that could not be evidenced in either are marked explicitly as not specified.

docs.title: How to use this site
docs.text:
A reasonable reading order for someone new to PIMS:

  1. Glossary — settle the terminology first; several terms have legacy synonyms still visible in the application.
  2. User Stories — the detailed specification, one story per capability, each with acceptance criteria.
  3. Business Rules — the numbered decision logic (BR-001 to BR-035) that the stories depend on.
  4. Process Flows and Sequence Diagrams — how the capabilities fit together, including failure paths.
  5. Implementation Conformance Matrix — which requirements are evidenced in the current implementation, and which are only partially evidenced.

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text: ID Assumption Source ASM-001 PIMS is built on Microsoft Dynamics 365 (Model-Driven App) and Azure Integration Services. All requirements assume these platforms remain in use. Across all stories ASM-002 TRACES Classic provides ITAHC and DOCOM data in a structured JSON format that can be consumed by Azure Logic Apps/Functions. Field mapping details remain to be agreed separately, so attribute-level traceability is incomplete until the schemas behind IMTA-6598, IMTA-6599, IMTA-6600 and IMTA-6601 are confirmed. IMTA-6598, IMTA-6599, IMTA-6600, IMTA-6601 ASM-003 IPAFFS provides Importer Notifications in JSON format via a push to an Azure Service Bus Queue. The implemented entity is Importer Notification, even where some legacy labels continue to use the term Import Notification. IMTA-5864, IMTA-7201 ASM-004 The Country reference data entity is sourced from the existing Exports solution (Microsoft Customer engagement) and is available for import into the EU Imports solution. IMTA-5915 ASM-005 Commodity Type reference data is sourced from the existing Defra Exports D365 solution and is available for import into the EU Imports solution. IMTA-5916 ASM-006 All caseworker users are authenticated via Azure Active Directory (Entra ID) with Dynamics 365. General ASM-007 TRACES service account auto-creation of ITAHC/DOCOM records uses a dedicated service principal whose identity is distinguishable from human users. This is required for the auto-create Import Record logic (IMTA-6600, IMTA-6601). IMTA-6600, IMTA-6601 ASM-008 The Devolved Office field on an Import Record reflects Scottish, Welsh and English routing. Geographic team assignment is configurable using out-of-the-box D365 Team records. IMTA-5863, IMTA-6661 ASM-009 Document attachment to Import Records uses the Azure Attachment Management solution (Microsoft Labs AppSource solution). IMTA-5913 ASM-010 Inspection Coverage Rule thresholds (e.g. "every 50th P3 record" ≈ 2%) are configurable by Dynamics 365 System Administrators. The configuration parameter defraimp_inspectionCoverageCount currently holds the value 50; actual policy value may be updated through Reference Data administration. IMTA-5891, IMTA-5892 ASM-011 The ITAHC/DOCOM "Replaced By / Replaces" chain mirrors the TRACES replacement logic. Exact status field values from TRACES are subject to mapping confirmation, and explicit primary-selection prevention for replaced certificates remains to be evidenced in all contexts. IMTA-5984 ASM-012 The FAET report (IMTA-6354) is an Excel export produced by a user with the Excel Export security role. The mechanics of export (Advanced Find export, custom report or Power BI) are not specified in the source stories and must be confirmed. IMTA-6354

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: ID Dependency Impact if Not Met DEP-001 TRACES Classic integration API/message format and field schemas must be agreed and stable. The TRACES-to-D365 field mapping schema is documented in the Defra - EU Imports - D365 - Entity Schemas workbook, which is held outside this repository. That workbook covers the complete ITAHC and DOCOM field mappings including mandatory fields, D365 schema names, transformations applied (e.g. JSON serialisation for Commodity Complements and Identification of Animals), and import record cross-mappings. Attribute-level traceability is resolvable for IMTA-6598 (ITAHC) and IMTA-6599 (DOCOM). IMTA-6600 and IMTA-6601 (CVED/other formats) are not covered by that workbook. DEP-002 IPAFFS integration message format (Importer Notification JSON schema) must be agreed and stable. Importer Notification receipt and processing (IMTA-5864) cannot be completed until schema is confirmed. DEP-003 Defra Exports D365 solution must be available to supply Country and Commodity Type reference data. Risk level rules (US-011, US-012) cannot be configured until reference data is available. DEP-004 Azure Integration Services infrastructure (Service Bus, Logic Apps) must be provisioned before integration stories can be delivered. IMTA-5862, IMTA-5864, IMTA-6598, IMTA-6599 DEP-005 Azure Attachment Management (Microsoft Labs) solution must be deployed before document attachment (US-029) can be configured. IMTA-5913 DEP-006 D365 Team records for geographic teams (IRMS Scotland, Wales, England) must be provisioned and replicated to all environments before geographic assignment (US-026) can function. IMTA-5863 Solution notes DEP-007 Whether IMTA-6662 requires a distinct automated ITAHC PDF-generation workflow, beyond generic document attachment, must be confirmed. Document-management scope and traceability for ITAHC PDFs remains ambiguous until this is resolved. DEP-009 Business Process Flow entry/exit criteria and transition constraints for Import Records must be documented explicitly if they are required beyond the implemented stage names. Stage names are known, but some downstream documents cannot provide full transition-rule traceability until this detail is confirmed. DEP-010 The future-state IV66 lifecycle described in IMTA-6132 must be confirmed as in scope or out of scope. If in scope, additional requirements will be needed for the registrant submission-to-feedback loop. DEP-011 Authoritative extracts for EICM-34 and EICM-37 must be obtained. Random-inspection traceability remains incomplete for references inherited from external Jira stories.

docs.title: Technical Constraints
docs.text: ID Constraint Source CON-001 PIMS is constrained to Microsoft Dynamics 365 Model-Driven App patterns (Plugins, Custom Workflow Activities, Business Rules, JavaScript Web Resources). Custom portals or standalone services are out of scope. Platform constraint CON-002 Business logic must be implemented as synchronous Plugins or Custom Workflow Activities for risk assessment rules to ensure data consistency on record save. IMTA-5866, IMTA-5892, IMTA-5895 Solution notes CON-003 Auto-number fields in Dynamics 365 cannot guarantee gapless sequences in all failure scenarios. The unique reference number (BR-022) and query number (BR-023) formats must account for this. IMTA-6132, IMTA-6185 CON-004 The D365 audit log must be enabled at both organisation and entity level before audit requirements (NFR-AUD-001, NFR-AUD-002) can be satisfied. IMTA-5986, IMTA-6128 CON-005 Dashboards and reports are built using native D365 Charts, Views and Dashboards. Power BI or custom reporting tools are not referenced in the source stories. IMTA-6340, IMTA-6341, IMTA-6343, IMTA-6344, IMTA-6372

docs.title: Organisational Constraints
docs.text: ID Constraint Source ORG-001 Inspection Coverage Rule thresholds (2% P3, 10% P2) are set by Defra policy. PIMS must implement them as configurable values but must not allow business users below System Administrator level to change them. IMTA-5891 AC-2 ORG-002 The EU Imports Business Rules Admin role is responsible for maintaining Commodity Risk Levels, Gold/Bronze Commodities and the unique reference number prefix. Changes must be auditable. IMTA-5865, IMTA-5888, IMTA-6132 ORG-003 Geographic team routing (Scotland, Wales, England) must reflect the actual organisational structure of the IRMS team and must be maintained in D365 Team records. IMTA-5863

docs.title: External System Constraints
docs.text: ID Constraint Source EXT-001 PIMS consumes messages from TRACES Classic and IPAFFS; it does not push data back to these systems. PIMS is a read-only consumer of external notifications. Inferred from all integration stories EXT-002 IPAFFS message delivery is asynchronous and event-driven (status change trigger: Submitted, Amended, Cancelled). PIMS must handle all three statuses as create-or-update operations. IMTA-5864 AC-1 EXT-003 TRACES Classic sends notifications by email to the CIT team. The integration intercepts this mechanism and routes data via Azure Service Bus. The email channel must remain available as a fallback. IMTA-6598 AC-1

docs.title: Business Rules
docs.text: All business rules are numbered sequentially. Each rule references the originating user story (US-xxx) and source Jira issues.

docs.title: BR-001 — Commodity Risk Level Determines Base Risk Level
docs.text:
When an Import Record is created or updated, PIMS must evaluate the configured Commodity Risk Level rules (Country × Commodity Type → Risk Level) to determine the base risk classification (P1, P2, P3) for the Import Record.

  • Source: US-011
  • Jira: IMTA-5865, IMTA-5914, IMTA-5915, IMTA-5916

docs.title: BR-002 — P1 with Gold/Bronze Commodity and Bronze Place of Origin → Post Import Check Required
docs.text:
When an Import Record is created or updated AND the Commodity Type + Country of Origin matches a Gold/Bronze Commodity rule AND the linked Place of Origin has Trust Level = Bronze, PIMS must set:

  • Post Import Checks Required? = Yes

  • Post Import Checks Required Reason = Bronze Place of Origin

  • Source: US-014

  • Jira: IMTA-5866 AC-1

docs.title: BR-003 — P1 with Gold/Bronze Commodity and Gold Place of Origin → Inspection at 1-in-10 Frequency
docs.text:
When an Import Record is created or updated AND the Commodity Type + Country of Origin matches a Gold/Bronze Commodity rule AND the linked Place of Origin has Trust Level = Gold AND the Number of Import Records Since Last Post Import Check ≥ 10, PIMS must set:

  • Post Import Checks Required? = Yes
  • Post Import Checks Required Reason = Gold Place of Origin — Inspection Coverage
  • Number of Import Records Since Last Post Import Check on the Place of Origin = 0

Otherwise:

  • Post Import Checks Required? = No

  • Post Import Checks Required Reason = No Inspection Required — Gold Place of Origin

  • Source: US-014

  • Jira: IMTA-5866 AC-2, AC-3

docs.title: BR-004 — P1 with Gold/Bronze Commodity but No Verified Place of Origin → Undetermined
docs.text:
When an Import Record is created or updated AND the Commodity Type + Country of Origin matches a Gold/Bronze Commodity rule AND no Place of Origin is linked to the Import Record, PIMS must set:

  • Post Import Checks Required? = Undetermined

  • Post Import Checks Required Reason = Verified Place of Origin Missing

  • Source: US-014

  • Jira: IMTA-5866 AC-4

docs.title: BR-005 — P1 with Gold/Bronze Commodity — Manual Override Reallocates 10th Inspection
docs.text:
When an Import Record has been flagged for a Post Import Check under BR-003 AND the user subsequently sets Post Import Checks Required? = No, PIMS must reallocate the missed inspection to the next Import Record associated with the same Place of Origin by adding 1 to the Number of Import Records Since Last Post Import Check counter.

  • Source: US-014
  • Jira: IMTA-5866 AC-5

docs.title: BR-006 — P1 Inspection — Gold/Bronze Rating Not Determinable → Discretionary
docs.text:
When the Risk Level is set to P1 AND the Gold/Bronze rating cannot be determined (no Gold/Bronze Commodity rule applies), the Post Import Check requirement is set to Discretionary with reason "Decision to inspect is discretionary".

  • Source: US-014
  • Jira: IMTA-5894

docs.title: BR-007 — P2 Random 10% Inspection Coverage
docs.text:
When an Import Record Risk Level is set or changed to P2:

  1. If the Import Record Priority 2 Quota Counter > 0: decrement the counter by 1 and flag the record for Post Import Check.
  2. Otherwise: increment the Import Record Priority 2 Counter. If the counter reaches the configured limit (10): reset the counter to 0 and flag the record for Post Import Check.

When an Import Record Risk Level is changed away from P2:

  • If the record was flagged for inspection: increment the Quota Counter by 1 (to schedule a replacement).

  • If the record was not flagged for inspection: decrement the Priority 2 Counter by 1 (to maintain the ratio).

  • Source: US-015

  • Jira: IMTA-5895

docs.title: BR-008 — P3 Random 2% Inspection Coverage (ITAHC Records Only)
docs.text:
When an Import Record of type ITAHC with a linked Primary ITAHC is created:

  1. Increment the "2% All Import Records — Random" Inspection Coverage Count value.
  2. If the count value equals or exceeds the configured limit: flag the Import Record for Post Import Check with reason "Random P3 Inspection" and reset the counter to 0.
  3. If the count is below the limit and the Risk Level is P3: set Post Import Checks Required? = No with reason "No inspection required".

The counter is only incremented on create, not on update.

This rule only applies to Import Records with Risk Level = P3.

  • Source: US-016
  • Jira: IMTA-5892

docs.title: BR-009 — Random Inspection Counter Incremented Before Risk Assessment
docs.text:
The Import Record Counter must be incremented before automated risk assessment rules are evaluated, to ensure accurate sequencing.

  • Source: US-016
  • Jira: IMTA-5867 AC-1

docs.title: Place of Origin Trust Level Rules
BR-010 — New Place of Origin Defaults to Bronze Trust Level
docs.text:
When a Place of Origin is created, its Trust Level must default to Bronze.

  • Source: US-018
  • Jira: IMTA-5886 AC-1

docs.title: BR-011 — Gold Trust Level Awarded After 3 Consecutive Satisfactory Outcomes
docs.text:
PIMS must promote the Trust Level of a Place of Origin from Bronze to Gold after 3 consecutive Import Records are completed with a Post Import Check Outcome of Satisfactory or Not Visited, provided the Place of Origin is not locked to Bronze.

  • Source: US-018
  • Jira: IMTA-5886 AC-3

docs.title: BR-012 — Consecutive Satisfactory Count Resets on Unsatisfactory Outcome
docs.text:
When an Import Record is completed with a Post Import Check Outcome of Unsatisfactory, PIMS must set the Number of Consecutive Satisfactory Import Records for the associated Place of Origin to 0.

  • Source: US-018
  • Jira: IMTA-5886 AC-2

docs.title: BR-013 — Trust Level Revoked to Bronze on Unsatisfactory Outcome + User Confirmation
docs.text:
When an Import Record is completed with Post Import Check Outcome = Unsatisfactory AND the user selects Reset Gold Trust Level to Bronze? = Yes, PIMS must set the Trust Level of the associated Place of Origin to Bronze.

  • Source: US-021
  • Jira: IMTA-5886 AC-4, IMTA-6669

docs.title: BR-014 — Lock to Bronze Prevents Automatic Gold Promotion
docs.text:
When a Place of Origin has Lock to Bronze = Yes, BR-011 must not be applied. The Trust Level remains Bronze regardless of consecutive satisfactory outcomes.

  • Source: US-019
  • Jira: IMTA-5890 AC-2

docs.title: BR-015 — Unlock from Bronze Restores Previous Trust Level
docs.text:
When the Lock to Bronze field is changed from Yes to No, PIMS must restore the Trust Level to the value stored in the Previous Trust Level field.

  • Source: US-019, US-020
  • Jira: IMTA-6668

docs.title: BR-016 — Lock to Bronze Requires a Mandatory Reason
docs.text:
When the Lock to Bronze field is set to Yes, the user must provide a non-empty value in the Locked to Bronze Reason field before the record can be saved.

  • Source: US-019
  • Jira: IMTA-5890 AC-5

docs.title: BR-017 — Unlock from Bronze Requires a Mandatory Reason
docs.text:
When the Lock to Bronze field is changed from Yes to No, the user must provide a non-empty value in the Unlocked from Lock to Bronze Reason field before the record can be saved.

  • Source: US-019
  • Jira: IMTA-5890 AC-7

docs.title: BR-018 — Number of Import Records Counter on Place of Origin Incremented on Link
docs.text:
The Number of Import Records counter on a Place of Origin must be incremented by 1 when an Import Record is linked to the Place of Origin and the Import Record has a Primary ITAHC. It must be decremented by 1 when the link is removed or the Primary ITAHC is cleared.

  • Source: US-018
  • Jira: IMTA-5886 AC-5

docs.title: BR-019 — Number of Import Records Since Last Check Counter Incremented for Gold Places of Origin
docs.text:
For Import Records with a Gold/Bronze Commodity and a Place of Origin with Trust Level = Gold: PIMS must increment the Number of Import Records Since Last Check counter on the Place of Origin by 1 each time the Import Record is completed.

  • Source: US-018
  • Jira: IMTA-5886 AC-6

docs.title: BR-020 — Changing Place of Origin Updates Previous Place of Origin Counters
docs.text:
When the Verified Place of Origin on an Import Record is changed:

  1. Decrement the Number of Import Records counter on the previous Place of Origin by 1.
  2. If the previous Place of Origin was Gold and the Import Record was flagged for a Gold inspection: add 1 to the previous Place of Origin's Inspection Quota.

  3. Re-evaluate the Post Import Check requirement based on the new Place of Origin.

  4. Source: US-020

  5. Jira: IMTA-6666

docs.title: BR-021 — Manual Early Post Import Check Resets Gold Counter
docs.text:
When a user manually sets Post Import Check Required? = Yes on an Import Record where the previous value was No and the Place of Origin Trust Level = Gold and the Number of Import Records Since Last Post Import Check is between 1 and 9 (inclusive), PIMS must reset the counter to 0.

  • Source: US-022
  • Jira: IMTA-6680

docs.title: BR-022 — Unique Reference Number Format
docs.text:
The unique reference number generated for each Import Record must follow the format: GB.{YEAR}.{9-digit-sequential-number} Example: GB.2019.000000009

The prefix (default GB.) must be configurable by an EU Imports Business Rules Admin.

  • Source: US-028
  • Jira: IMTA-6132

docs.title: BR-023 — Import Query Number Format
docs.text:
The unique reference number generated for each Import Query must follow the format: RMQ{YY}-{4-digit-sequential-number} Example: RMQ19-0024

The sequence number must be global across all Import Queries (not per-Import-Record).

  • Source: US-025
  • Jira: IMTA-6185, IMTA-6255

docs.title: BR-024 — IV65 Response Due Date = IV65 Sent Date + 14 Calendar Days
docs.text:
When a user changes the IV65 Sent Date field, PIMS must automatically calculate IV65 Response Due Date = IV65 Sent Date + 14 calendar days. The calculated date remains editable by caseworkers.

  • Source: US-030
  • Jira: IMTA-6166

docs.title: BR-025 — Warble Fly Treatment Declaration Received Date Only Enabled When Required
docs.text:
The Warble Fly Treatment Declaration Received Date field must be enabled only when Warble Fly Treatment Declaration Required? = Yes. If the user changes the value back to No, the Received Date must be cleared and the field disabled.

  • Source: US-032
  • Jira: IMTA-6158

docs.title: BR-026 — Moved to Completion Date Journalled Automatically
docs.text:
When a user sets the Moved to Completion? field to Yes, PIMS must record the current date and time in the Moved to Completion Date field (read-only). When the field is set back to No, the date must be cleared.

  • Source: US-031
  • Jira: IMTA-6180

docs.title: BR-027 — ITAHC/DOCOM Status and Replacement Chain Must Be Tracked
docs.text:
The Replaced By and Replaces fields on ITAHC and DOCOM records must reflect the replacement chain from TRACES. Current implementation evidence confirms the replacement links and cross-references are maintained. Explicit prevention of primary-certificate selection in every user interaction context is not yet fully evidenced and requires confirmation.

  • Source: US-002
  • Jira: IMTA-5984

docs.title: BR-028 — "No ITAHC Received" Option on Import Record
docs.text:
A user must be able to select "No ITAHC Received" in the Primary ITAHC lookup on an Import Record to allow the record to be saved without a linked ITAHC. Source stories may refer to this option as "No ITAHC Provided".

  • Source: US-001
  • Jira: IMTA-5985

docs.title: BR-029 — Deleted Importer Notification Attachments Remain Active
docs.text:
When an Importer Notification update from IPAFFS removes a related record (e.g. an Additional Permanent Address), the equivalent record in PIMS must remain active and not be deleted, as Import Records may already reference that data.

This rule applies to the implemented Importer Notification entity used for IPAFFS data. Legacy wording may still refer to some of these records or views as "Import Notification".

  • Source: US-006
  • Jira: IMTA-5864 AC-2

docs.title: BR-030 — Inspection Coverage Rules Configurable by Business Rules Admin Only
docs.text:
Inspection Coverage Rules must only be creatable or updatable by users with the Dynamics 365 System Administrator role. All other business user security roles, including EU Imports Business Rules Admin, must be restricted to read access only.

  • Source: US-013
  • Jira: IMTA-5891 AC-2

docs.title: BR-031 — Documents Attached to Import Records Cannot Be Deleted
docs.text:
An EU Imports Caseworker must not be able to delete documents once attached to an Import Record.

  • Source: US-029
  • Jira: IMTA-5913 AC-3

docs.title: BR-032 — Import Query Notes Can Be Added by Non-Owners
docs.text:
An EU Imports Caseworker must be able to attach notes and files to an Import Query even if they are not the owner of that query.

  • Source: US-025
  • Jira: IMTA-6185 AC-7

docs.title: BR-033 — Inbound IPAFFS Messages That Fail Processing Go to Dead Letter Queue
docs.text:
If an Importer Notification received from IPAFFS cannot be created or updated in PIMS, the failed message must be placed on the Dead Letter Queue.

  • Source: US-006
  • Jira: IMTA-5864 AC-3

docs.title: BR-034 — IPAFFS Commodity Identifiers Must Be Translated to D365 Commodity Classification
docs.text:
When IPAFFS Importer Notification data is processed for downstream Import Record creation or update, PIMS must translate the IPAFFS commodity identifier to the D365 commodity classification using the configured Commodity Type Mapping.

  • Source: US-006
  • Jira: IMTA-7222

docs.title: BR-035 — Failed TRACES Receipts Must Be Captured, Visible and Reprocessable
docs.text:
If an inbound ITAHC or DOCOM receipt from TRACES Classic cannot be processed into PIMS, the failure must be captured with enough detail for investigation, exposed to authorised operational users for review, support controlled retry or reprocess actions, and maintain an auditable history of the failure and its resolution.

  • Source: US-047
  • Jira: IMTA-6626

docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: This glossary defines canonical terminology for PIMS. Where multiple terms were used inconsistently across source Jira stories, the preferred term is listed first and alternatives are noted.

docs.title: Business Terms
docs.text:
Term Definition Aliases / Notes Import Record The primary case record in PIMS representing a single consignment being risk-assessed. Contains links to health certificates, place of origin, risk level and post-import check requirements. Previously called "Import Application" in some stories. Use "Import Record" as the canonical term. The underlying D365 schema and some workflow artefact names may still use importapplication / "Import Application". ITAHC Intra-Trade Animal Health Certificate. The EU health certificate for live animals, raised in TRACES by the EU exporter. Always written ITAHC (the H is often dropped in speech, but never in writing). DOCOM Commercial Document. Used for low-risk movements such as animal by-products and one equine derogation. Simpler than an ITAHC. CVED Common Veterinary Entry Document. A certificate used for goods imported from third countries at a Border Inspection Post. Import Notification A legacy notification concept used for manual or non-TRACES pre-notifications (for example IV66-related notifications). Distinct from Importer Notification. The current implementation evidence does not show a separate dedicated Import Notification entity in solution metadata. The wording persists in some labels, views and dashboard text. Importer Notification A notification submitted by an importer via IPAFFS and automatically received by PIMS. Created by IMTA-5864 / IMTA-7201. This is the implemented D365 entity for IPAFFS-originated notifications. Some legacy labels and options may still use the older term "Import Notification". Post Import Check A physical or document-based inspection of a consignment conducted after it has entered the UK. May be triggered automatically by PIMS business rules or manually by a caseworker. Also referred to as "Post Import Inspection" in informal usage. Use "Post Import Check" as the canonical term. Place of Origin A registered premises from which consignments originate. PIMS maintains a Trust Level (Gold or Bronze) for each Place of Origin based on inspection history. Also referred to as "Premises of Origin" in some stories. Use "Place of Origin" as the canonical term. Trust Level The risk rating assigned to a Place of Origin. Values: Gold (low risk, verified compliance history) and Bronze (standard risk, default). Gold Trust Level Awarded to a Place of Origin after 3 consecutive satisfactory post-import check outcomes. Results in reduced inspection frequency (1-in-10 consignments). Bronze Trust Level The default Trust Level assigned to all new Places of Origin. Results in higher inspection frequency. Lock to Bronze A manual override that prevents PIMS from automatically promoting a Place of Origin's Trust Level from Bronze to Gold. Import Query A formal query raised by a caseworker against an Import Record, directed to the importer or a third party. Tracked through creation, assignment and resolution. Match Record A system-supported matching artefact used to identify candidate related Import Records for inbound certificates or notifications. Supports matching workflows and the "Match View", including display of Work Schedule Number where available. Risk Level The automated risk classification applied to an Import Record. Values: P1 (high risk), P2 (medium risk / low risk commercial), P3 (low risk). P1 High-risk Import Record. Post-import check requirement determined by Gold/Bronze commodity rules. P2 Medium-risk Import Record. Subject to the 10% random post-import check coverage rule. P3 Low-risk Import Record. Subject to the 2% random post-import check coverage rule. Commodity Risk Level A configurable rule that maps a Country + Commodity Type combination to a Risk Level (P1, P2, P3). Also called "Import Country Commodity Risk Level" in early stories. Gold/Bronze Commodity A commodity type (and optional country list) for which the Gold/Bronze Place of Origin trust level rules apply. Inspection Coverage Rule A configurable rule defining the threshold count at which a random inspection must be triggered. Rules are named and associated to risk levels (e.g., "10% Rule" for P2, "2% All-Case-Random" for P3, "Gold Commodity Every X" for Gold commodities). Thresholds are stored as whole numbers (Number of Records Until Inspection) and are managed by System Administrators. US-013 Inspection Coverage Count A counter tracking the number of Import Records processed since the last random inspection was triggered for a given coverage rule. Post Import Check Outcome The result of a post-import check. Values include: Satisfactory, Not Visited, Unsatisfactory, Non-Compliant, Resolved Not Required, Cancelled, Quarantined, Additional Inspection Required. IV65 A formal written query sent from Defra to a place of origin or consignor. Has a 14-day response due date. IV66 The paper Import Notification Form (form reference IV66(ES), issued under The Trade in Animals and Related Products Regulations 2011) completed by importers to notify Defra of an incoming consignment. Captures importer details, country of origin, transiting countries, date of import, place of destination, premises of origin, species/product, quantity, and port of entry. The IV66 paper process is the predecessor to digital submission via IPAFFS. In the current system, pre-notification data arrives as an Importer Notification via IPAFFS rather than through the paper form; manual Import Records may still be created for IV66 edge cases. Previously incorrectly described as "Creates an Import Notification in PIMS" — IV66 is the source form, not a PIMS record type. IV17 A document associated with Post Import Check processing. Warble Fly Treatment Declaration A declaration confirming that cattle consignments have been treated for warble fly prior to import. docs.title: 1. Business Objectives
docs.text:
1. Replace manual, paper-based and spreadsheet-driven EU imports case management processes with a centralised, auditable digital system.
  2. Ensure consistent application of Defra policy for risk-based post-import checks on animal and commodity consignments entering the UK from the EU.
  3. Reduce the administrative burden on EU Imports Caseworkers by automating risk assessment, inspection flagging and counter management.
  4. Provide real-time operational visibility for team leaders and managers through dashboards and reports.
  5. Maintain full auditability of all case decisions for regulatory compliance purposes.
  6. Integrate with external veterinary and import notification systems (TRACES Classic, IPAFFS) to eliminate duplicate data entry.

docs.title: 2. Product Vision
docs.text:
PIMS (Post Import Management System) is a Dynamics 365-based case management platform that:

  • Receives consignment health certificate data automatically from TRACES Classic (ITAHC, DOCOM) and importer notification data from IPAFFS.
  • Uses the implemented Importer Notification processing flow to support downstream Import Record creation, matching and risk assessment activities.
  • Enables caseworkers to create, manage and complete Import Records across the full lifecycle from initial triage through to post-import check outcome.
  • Applies configurable business rules to automatically determine the risk level and post-import check requirement for every consignment.
  • Provides team leaders, managers and reporting teams with dashboards and exportable reports to meet Defra operational and policy reporting requirements.

docs.title: 6. Success Criteria
docs.text:
# Criterion 1 ITAHC and DOCOM records are automatically created in PIMS within the agreed processing window of creation in TRACES Classic 2 Importer Notifications from IPAFFS are received and processed within the agreed processing window 3 Automated risk assessment correctly classifies 100% of Import Records according to configured rules 4 Random inspection coverage (2% P3, 10% P2) is applied consistently and auditably 5 All field changes on Import Records and Post Import Checks are captured in the audit trail 6 Caseworkers can complete core workflows (create Import Record, link Place of Origin, flag for post-import check) without manual re-keying of health certificate data 7 Dashboards provide near-real-time operational data without external tooling 8 Every business decision is traceable to a configurable rule

The processing-window and coverage figures behind criteria 1, 2 and 4 are specified once, as measurable targets, in the Non-Functional Requirements (NFR-PER-* and NFR-COM-*). They are not restated here.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Ensure that all case decisions, field changes, inspection decisions and counter changes in PIMS are fully audited and traceable to demonstrate regulatory compliance.

docs.title: Business Value
docs.text:

  • Counter history provides transparency into why automated inspection flags were raised.

docs.title: Capability Description
docs.text:
PIMS enables full auditability through:

  • D365 organisation-level auditing on Import Records and Post Import Checks
  • Unique reference number generation for all Import Records
  • Counter History entity tracking every increment/decrement/reset of risk and trust level counters

docs.title: Functional Scope
docs.text:
• Enable D365 audit log on Import Record and Post Import Check entities and all custom fields
  • Generate unique reference numbers for Import Records (format: GB.{YEAR}.{9-digit-sequence})
  • Record Counter History for all risk assessment counters (P1/P2/P3 auto-number counters)
  • Record Counter History for all Place of Origin trust level counters
  • Each Counter History entry records: Import Record, counter type, operation, reason, previous value, current value

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Enable EU Imports Caseworkers to create, manage and complete all types of consignment health certificate records and the Import Record that links them, throughout the full case lifecycle.

docs.title: Business Value
docs.text: Caseworkers can manage the complete EU imports workflow within a single system, replacing fragmented paper and spreadsheet processes with a traceable, auditable digital record.

docs.title: Capability Description
docs.text:
PIMS provides caseworkers with the ability to create and manage the following record types:

  • Import Record — the primary case record linking health certificates, place of origin, risk assessment and post-import check
  • ITAHC — International Transport of Animals Health Certificate
  • DOCOM — Document of Commercial Movement
  • CVED — Common Veterinary Entry Document
  • Import Notification — legacy pre-notification wording retained in some labels, views and dashboard text
  • Importer Notification — the implemented IPAFFS-sourced notification entity (auto-received)
  • Match Record — matching support artefact used to identify candidate related Import Records

Supporting case management capabilities include document attachment, IV65 response tracking, warble fly declaration tracking, completion date recording, matching support and quick-create for triage. Business-facing requirements use Import Record as the canonical term, while some technical artefacts still use importapplication / "Import Application".

docs.title: Functional Scope
docs.text:
• Create, update, view, list and search for Import Records, ITAHCs, DOCOMs, CVEDs and Import Notifications
  • Link health certificates to Import Records
  • Attach documents to Import Records
  • Calculate IV65 response due dates
  • Record warble fly treatment declaration dates
  • Record Import Record completion dates
  • Quick-create Import Records for the unassigned work queue
  • View Importer Notifications received from IPAFFS
  • Select "No ITAHC Received" on an Import Record where applicable
  • Review Match View candidates and Work Schedule Number context when matching inbound records

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Automate the receipt of health certificate data from TRACES Classic (ITAHC, DOCOM) and importer notification data from IPAFFS into PIMS, eliminating manual re-keying and enabling timely risk assessment.

docs.title: Business Value
docs.text:
• Caseworkers save significant time previously spent manually entering data from PDF certificates and email notifications.
  • Time saved can be redirected to risk assessment activities that reduce biological risk.
  • Consignments are processed faster and more consistently.
  • Failed messages are captured for investigation, preventing silent data loss.

docs.title: Capability Description
docs.text:
PIMS integrates with two external systems:

  1. TRACES Classic — sends ITAHC and DOCOM health certificate data to PIMS via Azure Integration Services (Service Bus, Logic Apps). Associated workflows create PIMS certificate records, support downstream Import Record creation, and require explicit failed-receipt handling when processing does not complete successfully.
  2. IPAFFS — sends Importer Notification data to PIMS via Azure Service Bus when an importer submits, amends or cancels a pre-notification. PIMS creates or updates the implemented Importer Notification entity accordingly, supports downstream Import Record creation/update workflows from that data, and routes failed messages to a Dead Letter Queue.

docs.title: Functional Scope
docs.text:
• Provision Azure Service Bus Queues for TRACES and IPAFFS inbound channels
  • Receive and process ITAHC and DOCOM data from TRACES Classic within 30 minutes
  • Automatically create ITAHC and DOCOM records in PIMS from TRACES data
  • Automatically create a linked Import Record when an ITAHC or DOCOM is received from TRACES
  • Receive and process Importer Notification data from IPAFFS (Submitted, Amended, Cancelled) within 30 minutes
  • Create or update Importer Notification records in PIMS from IPAFFS data
  • Translate IPAFFS commodity identifiers to D365 commodity classification using Commodity Type Mapping
  • Preserve related records on PIMS even when the IPAFFS update removes them (see BR-029)
  • Route failed IPAFFS messages to the Dead Letter Queue (BR-033)
  • Capture, expose and support controlled reprocessing of failed TRACES receipts (BR-035)

docs.title: Epic: Place of Origin Trust Level
Purpose
docs.text: Enable caseworkers to manage Places of Origin and allow PIMS to automatically maintain Trust Levels (Gold/Bronze) based on post-import check outcomes, to support risk-based inspection decisions.

docs.title: Business Value
docs.text:
• Trusted, repeatedly compliant places of origin receive reduced inspection frequency (1-in-10), reducing unnecessary inspections.
  • Non-compliant or unknown places of origin receive increased inspection frequency, protecting UK biosecurity.
  • Transparent, auditable trust level decisions with full counter history.

docs.title: Capability Description
docs.text:
PIMS maintains a Place of Origin registry. Each Place of Origin has a Trust Level (Gold or Bronze) and a set of counters tracking:

  • Number of consecutive satisfactory outcomes (used for Gold promotion)
  • Number of Import Records linked to the Place of Origin
  • Number of Import Records since the last post-import check

Rules govern automatic Trust Level transitions: - New Places of Origin default to Bronze. - 3 consecutive satisfactory outcomes promote a Place of Origin to Gold. - An unsatisfactory outcome resets the consecutive count to 0. - A caseworker can manually lock a Place of Origin to Bronze (with a mandatory reason). - Gold Trust Level can be revoked to Bronze following an unsatisfactory outcome (caseworker decision). - Counter changes are audited with reasons via the Counter History entity.

docs.title: Functional Scope
docs.text:
• Create and update Places of Origin
  • Search for a Place of Origin by name or postcode
  • Link a Place of Origin to an Import Record (lookup with Country of Origin auto-population)
  • Update the Place of Origin on an existing Import Record (with counter adjustment)
  • View related Import Records from a Place of Origin
  • Automatic Trust Level maintenance (Bronze default, Gold promotion, Bronze demotion)
  • Lock to Bronze with mandatory reason and audit record
  • Unlock from Bronze with mandatory reason and restoration of previous Trust Level
  • Revoke Gold Trust Level to Bronze after unsatisfactory outcome
  • Defer post-import check counter when manual inspection scheduled early
  • Full counter history tracking

  • Record the outcome of a Post Import Check.

  • View and filter Post Import Check records (due today, this week, this month)

  • Manually skip a system-required Post Import Check (with declined reason)

Purpose
docs.text: Enable EU Imports Business Rules Admins to configure and maintain the rules that PIMS uses to automatically classify Import Records by risk level and determine whether a post-import check is required.

docs.title: Business Value
docs.text:
• Consistent, auditable and policy-compliant risk classification on every Import Record.

  • Configurable rules allow policy changes to be applied without code releases.

docs.title: Capability Description
docs.text:
PIMS automatically determines the risk level (P1, P2, P3) and post-import check requirement for each Import Record based on:

  • Commodity Risk Levels — configurable rules mapping Country + Commodity Type to a Risk Level.
  • Gold/Bronze Commodity rules — define which commodity types (and optionally countries) are subject to Place of Origin trust level-based inspection logic.
  • Inspection Coverage Rules — define the random inspection thresholds:
  • 2% of all P3 ITAHC Import Records (every ~50th record)
  • 10% of all P2 Import Records (every 10th record)
  • P1 Discretionary — where a Gold/Bronze determination cannot be made, the inspection decision is left to caseworker discretion.

All rules are managed through Dynamics 365 entities with appropriate security role restrictions.

docs.title: Functional Scope
docs.text:
• Create and update Commodity Risk Level records (Country × Commodity Type → Risk Level)
  • View and select Countries from reference data
  • View and select Commodity Types from reference data
  • Create and update Gold/Bronze Commodity records (Commodity Type + Country list)
  • Update Inspection Coverage Rules (System Administrator only)
  • Automatic risk assessment on Import Record create/update:
  • Evaluate Commodity Risk Level rules to set Risk Level
  • Evaluate Gold/Bronze rules and Place of Origin Trust Level to determine Post Import Check requirement
  • Apply 10% P2 random inspection counter
  • Apply 2% P3 random inspection counter (ITAHC records only)
  • Set Post Import Checks Required? and Post Import Checks Required Reason on Import Record

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The Import Record is the primary case record in PIMS. It consolidates information from health certificates (ITAHC, DOCOM, CVED), import notifications and place of origin data into a single record that supports the full case lifecycle: Triage → Risk Assessment → Post Import Check → Completion.

docs.title: US-006: Receive Importer Notification from IPAFFS
Summary
docs.text: As an EU Imports Caseworker, I want PIMS to automatically receive Importer Notifications from IPAFFS when submitted by an importer, So that PIMS can create or update the implemented notification record, support matching to related certificates and Import Records, and commence a risk assessment.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
PIMS receives Importer Notifications from IPAFFS via an Azure Service Bus Queue. Messages are triggered by IPAFFS when a notification status changes to Submitted, Amended or Cancelled. PIMS processes each message to create or update the corresponding Importer Notification record. Failed messages are routed to the Dead Letter Queue.

IPAFFS notification types received by PIMS: CVEDA, CVEDP, CED, IMP. The full set of IPAFFS notification statuses is: DRAFT, SUBMITTED, VALIDATED, REJECTED, IN_PROGRESS, AMEND, MODIFY, REPLACED, CANCELLED, DELETED. PIMS processes messages for the statuses relevant to caseworker activity (Submitted, AMEND/MODIFY, Cancelled). Importer Notifications also carry replaces and replacedBy reference fields supporting amendment chain tracking, parallel to the TRACES ITAHC replacement model.

The Importer Notification entity is distinct from the legacy Import Notification concept (US-003). For the PIMS form and security role configuration related to viewing these records, see US-044.

The implemented IPAFFS flow uses the Importer Notification as the inbound entity and supports downstream Import Record creation or update workflows from that data. Earlier spike wording that described IPAFFS as creating ITAHC records is treated as legacy wording rather than the implemented solution shape.

Related records (e.g. Additional Permanent Addresses) that are removed in an IPAFFS update are retained in PIMS as active records, as they may already be referenced by Import Records. IPAFFS commodity identifiers are translated to the D365 commodity classification using Commodity Type Mapping to support downstream case processing.

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
• AC-1: When an Importer Notification in IPAFFS is created or updated with status Submitted, Amended or Cancelled, IPAFFS sends a JSON message to PIMS within 30 minutes.

  • AC-2: When an Importer Notification message is received from IPAFFS, PIMS creates or updates the corresponding Importer Notification record with all mapped attributes. Field updates are reflected on the record; cleared fields are captured in the audit history rather than overwriting data.

  • AC-3: When an IPAFFS update removes a previously present related record (e.g. an Additional Permanent Address), the equivalent PIMS record remains active and is not deleted.

  • AC-4: When an IPAFFS update modifies a related record, the change is reflected in the equivalent PIMS record.

  • AC-5: When an IPAFFS update introduces a new related record, a new equivalent PIMS record is created.

  • [~] AC-6: If the processing of an inbound IPAFFS message fails, the message is placed on the Dead Letter Queue for manual investigation.

  • AC-7: When IPAFFS commodity identifiers are used for downstream Import Record processing, PIMS translates them to the D365 commodity classification using Commodity Type Mapping.

docs.text:
• BR-029 — Related records retained on PIMS even when removed from IPAFFS update
  • BR-033 — Failed IPAFFS messages go to Dead Letter Queue
  • BR-034 — IPAFFS commodity identifiers translated to D365 commodity classification

docs.title: US-014: Automated Risk Assessment — P1 Consignments
Summary
docs.text: As an EU Imports Caseworker, I want PIMS to automatically determine whether a Post Import Check is required for a P1 Import Record based on Gold/Bronze commodity and Place of Origin trust level rules, So that Post Import Checks can be consistently scheduled based on policy.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
For Import Records classified as P1 (high risk), PIMS evaluates whether a Gold/Bronze Commodity rule applies and, if so, what the Trust Level of the linked Place of Origin is. Based on this evaluation, PIMS sets the Post Import Checks Required? field and the Post Import Checks Required Reason.

If the Gold/Bronze rule applies but no verified Place of Origin is linked, the requirement is set to Undetermined.

If no Gold/Bronze rule applies, the inspection decision is flagged as Discretionary.

Where a Gold inspection is triggered but the caseworker subsequently overrides it to No, the 10th-inspection obligation is reallocated to the next Import Record for the same Place of Origin.

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
• AC-1 (P1, Gold/Bronze commodity, Bronze Place of Origin → Post Import Check required): When an Import Record has Risk Level = P1 AND matches a Gold/Bronze Commodity rule AND the linked Place of Origin Trust Level = Bronze:
  • Post Import Checks Required? = Yes

  • Post Import Checks Required Reason = Bronze Place of Origin

  • AC-2 (P1, Gold/Bronze commodity, Gold Place of Origin, counter ≥ 10 → Post Import Check required): When an Import Record has Risk Level = P1 AND matches a Gold/Bronze Commodity rule AND the linked Place of Origin Trust Level = Gold AND Number of Import Records Since Last Post Import Check ≥ 10:

  • Post Import Checks Required? = Yes
  • Post Import Checks Required Reason = Gold Place of Origin — Inspection Coverage

  • Number of Import Records Since Last Post Import Check on the Place of Origin is reset to 0

  • AC-3 (P1, Gold/Bronze commodity, Gold Place of Origin, counter < 10 → No inspection required): When an Import Record has Risk Level = P1 AND matches a Gold/Bronze Commodity rule AND the linked Place of Origin Trust Level = Gold AND the counter is < 10:

  • Post Import Checks Required? = No

  • Post Import Checks Required Reason = No Inspection Required — Gold Place of Origin

  • AC-4 (P1, Gold/Bronze commodity, no Place of Origin → Undetermined): When an Import Record has Risk Level = P1 AND matches a Gold/Bronze Commodity rule AND no Place of Origin is linked:

  • Post Import Checks Required? = Undetermined

  • Post Import Checks Required Reason = Verified Place of Origin Missing

  • AC-5 (P1, no Gold/Bronze rule applies → Discretionary): When Risk Level = P1 AND no Gold/Bronze Commodity rule applies:

  • Post Import Checks Required? = Discretionary

  • Post Import Checks Required Reason = Decision to inspect is discretionary

  • AC-6 (Manual override of Gold inspection reallocates to next Import Record): When an Import Record was flagged under AC-2 and the user subsequently sets Post Import Checks Required? = No:

  • Number of Import Records Since Last Post Import Check on the Place of Origin is incremented by 1

docs.text:
• BR-002 — Bronze Place of Origin → check required
  • BR-003 — Gold Place of Origin, counter ≥ 10 → check required
  • BR-004 — No Place of Origin → Undetermined
  • BR-005 — Manual override reallocates 10th inspection
  • BR-006 — No Gold/Bronze rule → Discretionary

docs.title: US-015: Automated Risk Assessment — P2 Random 10%
Summary
docs.text: As an EU Imports Caseworker, I want PIMS to flag whether the Defra policy-based 10% P2 random inspection rule applies to Import Records, So that I can schedule a Post Import Check if required.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
PIMS applies the 10% P2 inspection coverage rule using two counters (Auto Numbers in the Reference Data area): - Import Application Priority 2 Counter — counts Import Records since the last P2 inspection. - Import Application Priority 2 Quota Counter — tracks inspections owed due to cases that were previously flagged for inspection but subsequently had their Risk Level changed away from P2.

The rule runs whenever an Import Record's Risk Level is set to or changed from P2. If a case moves from P2 before being inspected, the inspection obligation is preserved for a future case.

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
• AC-1 (On deployment): Two counters are initialised: Import Application Priority 2 Counter = 0 and Import Application Priority 2 Quota Counter = 0.

  • AC-2 (Risk Level changed to P2 — Quota Counter > 0): Decrement the Quota Counter by 1. Flag the Import Record for Post Import Check:

  • Post Import Checks Required? = Yes

  • Post Import Checks Required Reason = 10% P2-Case Rule

  • AC-3 (Risk Level changed to P2 — Quota Counter = 0, counter below limit): Increment the Import Application Priority 2 Counter by 1. Do not flag for inspection.

  • AC-4 (Risk Level changed to P2 — Quota Counter = 0, counter reaches limit of 10): Reset the Import Application Priority 2 Counter to 0. Flag the Import Record for Post Import Check:

  • Post Import Checks Required? = Yes

  • Post Import Checks Required Reason = 10% P2-Case Rule

  • AC-5 (Risk Level changed away from P2 — record was flagged for inspection): Increment the Quota Counter by 1 (to ensure a future case covers this inspection).

  • AC-6 (Risk Level changed away from P2 — record was not flagged for inspection): Decrement the Priority 2 Counter by 1 (to maintain the inspection ratio; counter can go negative).

  • [~] AC-7 (Bulk rebalancing): If the Quota Counter > 0 AND the Priority 2 Counter ≤ -10: decrement the Quota Counter by 1 and add 10 to the Priority 2 Counter.

docs.title: US-016: Automated Risk Assessment — P3 Random 2%
Summary
docs.text: As a Caseworker, I want PIMS to automatically flag a proportion of all P3 ITAHC Import Records for random inspection, So that we consistently inspect a random proportion of imported commodities aligned to current Defra policy.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
PIMS applies the 2% random inspection coverage rule to all P3 Import Records of type ITAHC with a Primary ITAHC linked. A single Auto Number counter (Import Application Priority 3 Counter, visible under Reference Data > Auto Numbers) is maintained, incremented on creation (not update) of qualifying Import Records. When the counter reaches the configured threshold (defined by the "2% All-Case-Random" Inspection Coverage Rule), the record is flagged for inspection and the counter resets to 0.

The counter increment happens before automated risk assessment rules are evaluated (BR-009).

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
• AC-1 (Counter incremented on qualifying Import Record creation): When an Import Record of type ITAHC with a linked Primary ITAHC is created (not updated), PIMS increments the Import Application Priority 3 Counter (Auto Number) by 1. This increment occurs before other risk assessment rules are evaluated.

  • AC-2 (Counter below threshold — no inspection flagged): If Risk Level = P3 AND the counter is less than the configured limit:

  • Post Import Checks Required? = No

  • Post Import Checks Required Reason = No inspection required

  • AC-3 (Counter reaches or exceeds threshold — inspection flagged, counter reset): If Risk Level = P3 AND the counter equals or exceeds the configured limit:

  • Post Import Checks Required? = Yes
  • Post Import Checks Required Reason = Random P3 Inspection

  • Counter is reset to 0

  • AC-4 (Rule only applies to P3): If Risk Level is not P3, the 2% rule does not apply and no Post Import Check is flagged under this rule.

  • BR-009 — Counter incremented before risk assessment evaluation

docs.title: US-018: Place of Origin Trust Level Maintenance
Summary
docs.text: As an EU Imports Caseworker, I want PIMS to automatically maintain the Trust Level of a Place of Origin based on the outcomes of Post Import Checks, So that when I create an Import Record and associate it with a Place of Origin, PIMS can automatically determine whether an inspection is required.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
PIMS automatically manages the Trust Level (Gold/Bronze) of each Place of Origin based on post-import check outcomes. Three counters are maintained per Place of Origin:

  1. Number of Consecutive Satisfactory Import Records — drives Gold promotion.
  2. Number of Import Records — tracks how many Import Records with a Primary ITAHC are linked.
  3. Number of Import Records Since Last Post Import Check — used by the Gold 1-in-10 inspection rule.

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
• AC-1: When a Place of Origin is created, its Trust Level defaults to Bronze.

  • AC-2 (Consecutive satisfactory count — increment): When an Import Record with a Gold/Bronze Commodity and a Place of Origin is completed with Post Import Check Outcome = Satisfactory or Not Visited, increment the Number of Consecutive Satisfactory Import Records for the Place of Origin by 1.

  • AC-3 (Consecutive satisfactory count — reset): When an Import Record with a Gold/Bronze Commodity and a Place of Origin is completed with Post Import Check Outcome = Unsatisfactory, reset the Number of Consecutive Satisfactory Import Records for the Place of Origin to 0.

  • AC-4 (Gold promotion after 3 consecutive satisfactory outcomes): After 3 consecutive Satisfactory or Not Visited outcomes, if the Place of Origin Trust Level is Bronze and Lock to Bronze = No, PIMS promotes the Trust Level to Gold.

  • AC-5 (Bronze demotion after unsatisfactory + Gold revocation): When a Post Import Check Outcome is Unsatisfactory AND the user sets Reset Gold Trust Level to Bronze? = Yes on the Import Record, PIMS sets the Trust Level to Bronze.

  • AC-6 (Number of Import Records — increment): When an Import Record with a Primary ITAHC is linked to a Place of Origin, increment the Number of Import Records counter on the Place of Origin by 1.

  • AC-7 (Number of Import Records — decrement): When a Place of Origin is unlinked from an Import Record, or the Primary ITAHC is cleared, decrement the Number of Import Records counter by 1.

  • AC-8 (Number of Import Records Since Last Check — increment): When an Import Record with a Gold/Bronze Commodity and a Gold Trust Level Place of Origin is completed, increment the Number of Import Records Since Last Post Import Check on the Place of Origin by 1.

docs.title: Business Rules
docs.text:
• BR-010 — Bronze default on creation
  • BR-011 — Gold promotion after 3 consecutive satisfactory outcomes
  • BR-012 — Consecutive count resets on Unsatisfactory
  • BR-013 — Trust Level revoked to Bronze on Unsatisfactory + user confirmation
  • BR-018 — Number of Import Records counter maintained
  • BR-019 — Number Since Last Check counter incremented for Gold Places of Origin

docs.title: US-019: Lock Place of Origin to Bronze
Summary
docs.text: As an EU Imports Caseworker, I want to be able to lock the Trust Level of a Place of Origin to Bronze, So that I can prevent PIMS from automatically promoting the Trust Level to Gold even after 3 consecutive satisfactory outcomes.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Provides caseworkers with a manual override to prevent a Place of Origin from being automatically promoted to Gold Trust Level. Locking requires a mandatory reason. Unlocking also requires a mandatory reason and restores the previous Trust Level. Both actions are audited.

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
• AC-1: An EU Imports Caseworker can set the Lock to Bronze field on a Place of Origin to Yes or No.

  • AC-2: While Lock to Bronze = Yes, PIMS does not promote the Trust Level to Gold regardless of the number of consecutive satisfactory outcomes.

  • AC-3: PIMS audits the user identity, date and time each time the Lock to Bronze field is changed.

  • AC-4: PIMS records the date when the Lock to Bronze field was last set to Yes in a field named Locked to Bronze Date (read-only, displayed next to the field).

  • AC-5: When the Lock to Bronze field is set to Yes, the user must provide a non-empty value in the Locked to Bronze Reason field before saving. PIMS prevents saving if this field is empty.

  • AC-6: PIMS records the date when the Lock to Bronze field was last changed from Yes to No in a field named Unlocked from Bronze Date.

  • AC-7: When the Lock to Bronze field is changed from Yes to No, the user must provide a non-empty value in the Unlocked from Lock to Bronze Reason field before saving.

  • AC-8: When the Lock to Bronze field is changed from Yes to No, PIMS restores the Trust Level to the value held in the Previous Trust Level field (see US-020 / BR-015).

  • AC-9: Before setting Lock to Bronze = Yes, PIMS records the current Trust Level in a read-only field named Previous Trust Level.

docs.text:
• BR-014 — Lock to Bronze prevents Gold promotion
  • BR-015 — Unlock from Bronze restores previous Trust Level
  • BR-016 — Locking requires a mandatory reason
  • BR-017 — Unlocking requires a mandatory reason

docs.text: As an EU Import Caseworker, I want to be able to manually skip or schedule a Post Import Check independently of what PIMS has determined, So that I can respond to import risks manually when the automated rules do not reflect the full picture.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Caseworkers can override PIMS's automated Post Import Check determination in both directions: skipping a system-required inspection (with a decline reason) or scheduling a check for a record not flagged by the system (with an explicit reason).

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
• AC-1 (Manually skip a system-required Post Import Check): An EU Imports Caseworker can activate a "Skip this Post Import Check" action on an Import Record that was flagged for a Post Import Check. This sets:
  • Post Import Checks Required? = No

  • Post Import Checks Declined Reason = System Required Post Import Check Skipped

  • AC-2 (Manually schedule a Post Import Check): An EU Imports Caseworker can activate a "Post Import Check this Record" action on an Import Record that was not flagged for a Post Import Check. This sets:

  • Post Import Checks Required? = Yes
  • Post Import Checks Required Reason = Manually Requested Post Import Check

docs.title: Business Rules
docs.text: • BR-021 — Manually scheduling an early Post Import Check resets the Gold counter (US-022)

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
• US-001 (Import Record)
  • US-022 (Counter deferral for early manual inspection)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: As an EU Imports Caseworker, I want to be able to create, track, assign and resolve Import Queries against Import Records, So that I can record formal queries to importers or third parties and monitor their resolution.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Import Queries are formal queries raised by caseworkers against Import Records, directed to importers or other relevant parties. They are managed as a custom activity entity in Dynamics 365, leveraging OOB activity features for Raised By, Raised Date, assignment and Close as Resolved.

Each query receives an auto-generated sequential query number in the format RMQ{YY}-{SEQNUM:4}.

Note: IMTA-6185 (using "Import Record") and IMTA-6255 (using "Import Application") are duplicate source records describing the same functionality. They are consolidated into this single story, using the canonical term "Import Record".

docs.title: Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
• AC-1 (Create/update Import Query): An EU Imports Caseworker can create or update an Import Query with the following fields:
  • Query Sent To (email address)
  • Summary (Mandatory)
  • Related Import Record (Mandatory)
  • Date Due to Be Resolved

  • Detailed Description of the Query

  • AC-2 (View related Import Record context): Within the Import Query form, the caseworker can view the following fields from the related Import Record:

  • The relevant Health Certificate (ITAHC/DOCOM)
  • Commodity Type
  • Place of Origin Country

  • Any additional Health Certificates

  • AC-3 (Auto-populated fields on creation): The following fields are auto-populated when an Import Query is created:

  • Date Raised = today's date
  • Who Raised the Query = the creating user

  • Query Number = auto-generated in format RMQ{YY}-{SEQNUM:4}, unique across all Import Queries

  • AC-4 (Global query views with filters): An EU Imports Caseworker can view all queries in the system filtered by:

  • All Active Queries
  • All Completed Queries
  • All Overdue Queries
  • All Queries (all statuses)
  • My Active Queries
  • My Completed Queries
  • My Overdue Queries
  • All My Queries

Queries are sorted by Query Number. Each view shows: Query Number, Related Import Record, Query Sent To, Who Raised the Query, Summary, Date Raised, Date Due, Completion Status, Resolution Date (if resolved).

  • AC-5 (Related query views within an Import Record): An EU Imports Caseworker can view all queries related to a specific Import Record within the Import Record, filtered by:
  • All Related Queries
  • Overdue Related Queries

Sorted by Query Number. Same fields as AC-4.

  • AC-6 (Search for queries): An EU Imports Caseworker can search for queries by Query Number or Import Record name.

  • AC-7 (Attach notes and files): An EU Imports Caseworker can attach notes and files to any Import Query, including queries they do not own. Notes and files record the date added and who added them.

  • AC-8 (Close as resolved): An EU Imports Caseworker can close an Import Query as resolved. PIMS records the resolution date automatically.

  • AC-9 (Assign to another caseworker): An EU Imports Caseworker can assign an Import Query to another EU Imports Caseworker.

docs.title: Business Rules
docs.text:
• BR-023 — Query number format: RMQ{YY}-{SEQNUM:4}
  • BR-032 — Notes can be added by non-owners

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: • US-001 (Import Record — queries are linked to Import Records)

This baseline has evidence for generic attachment capability, including storing PDF versions of ITAHCs as documents.   • AC-3 (Prevent document deletion): An EU Imports Caseworker cannot delete documents once they have been attached to an Import Record.

  • [~] AC-3: Authorised operational users can initiate a controlled retry or reprocess action for a failed TRACES receipt after corrective action has been taken.

  • AC-4: Retry and resolution activity for failed TRACES receipts is auditable.
